substeps.caption: The warehouse version: the VLM and the alloy line's floor machines on an open floor, pallet racking round the edge, served by MiR250 mobile bases each carrying a UR10e. The machines face one aisle from both sides instead of standing along a rail: a MiR250 can dock at any front that faces an aisle.

The main aisle is 3.0 m wide, MiR's figure for two MiR250s passing with the default safety setup; one needs 1.45 m and pivots in 1.8 m. The docks sit between the aisle and the machines, each taped with a camera target on a post, so a docked unit blocks nothing. The two chargers stand 0.58 m apart (MiR: at least 0.55 m to the side of each).

Two units leave their chargers on the routes they are given: unit 1 to the VLM's opening, unit 2 to the 100 kN Instron. Each leg starts and stops at the MiR250's 0.3 m/s^2, up to 1.5 m/s (it does 2.0).

Two units leave their chargers on the routes they are given: unit 1 to the VLM's opening, unit 2 to the 100 kN Instron. Each leg starts and stops at the MiR250's 0.3 m/s^2, up to 1.5 m/s (it does 2.0).

Docked. MiR's figures for docking to an L-marker: ±6 mm along, ±3 mm across, ±1° of yaw. One degree is 23 mm at the arm's 1.3 m reach, so the wrist camera reads the target and shifts the taught frame before the arm works.

Both units go back to charge: 10 to 90 % takes 52 min on a MiR Charge 48V (MiR).

The trade against the rail: every front on the floor is reachable and the floor stays free, but a dock comes back to within millimetres, not the rail's ±0.3 mm, so every station needs a target the arm checks before it works.
